title: Building Security Agents That Cannot Escape Their Trust Boundary
summary: The article discusses the challenges and solutions for securely integrating AI-driven security agents into live infrastructure. It emphasizes the risks of granting AI models direct access to critical systems and proposes a two-sided architecture (sandbox + action-gate) to enforce strict trust boundaries. This ensures the agent operates in a read-only mode by design, preventing unauthorized modifications or data leaks. The solution, Cynative, is open-source and runs within the user's environment, maintaining data sovereignty and reducing operational overhead.
key_points: AI models with direct infrastructure access pose security risks (e.g., hallucinations leading to data deletion or misconfigurations).
Traditional SaaS security products mitigate risks via data lakes but introduce trade-offs (cost, sync delays, data sovereignty).
Attacker-defender asymmetry is exacerbated by attackers using advanced AI models and coding agents.
Least-privilege read-only access is necessary but insufficient due to potential IAM drift in large organizations.
Cynative's architecture includes a sandbox (isolated execution) and an action-gate (policy-enforced authorization) to enforce trust boundaries.
The agent is read-only by construction, preventing runtime boundary expansion or data exfiltration.
Cynative is deployed as a single binary within the user's environment, ensuring data sovereignty and compatibility with cloud-provider models.
Open-source framework allows customization for deep infrastructure research or building proprietary security agents.
